short: Ctrl C, Ctrl V. Wow, engineer.
medium: Pay Stack Overflow a salary. They wrote your whole project.
You copied the code. Now buy a subscription to understand it, bro.
Enough, bro. I haven't copy-pasted this much even in my past life.
long: What garbage code is this! Wait, you didn't even write it. You stole it from the internet and never read the comments.
I just remembered my past life. We read documentation back then. Now you people paste answers and call yourselves senior developers.

short: Deploy it already! Oh. It crashed.
Production is gone. So is your dignity.
medium: The server took one look at your code and resigned.
Read the logs. Even God won't debug that stack trace for you.
Works on my machine? Then courier your laptop to the customer.
long: Deploy it already, I told you! Now roll back the code, and roll back your dignity while you're at it.
I just remembered my past life. People like you deployed on Friday evenings, and I stayed awake all night.

short: Your cursor is tired of blinking.
medium: You've been staring at the screen forever. Write code, meditate later.
A calendar is not decoration, bro. The deadline is close.
Even your code isn't this idle. Oh wait, it doesn't run at all.
long: Check the clock, developer. The deadline won't wait for you. It's coming to haunt you instead.
If procrastination had a production build, you'd be CTO by now. Type something, or I'll sit on your keyboard.

short: It's a terminal, not a slot machine.
medium: Same code, same error, same confused face. Break the loop.
Try reading the error message, bro. It's free.
Add one print statement. Guessing isn't debugging.
long: I just remembered my past life. I stared at one bug for four hours, and the bug stared back.
Expecting new results from the same code? Debug first, run later. The bug won't leave out of embarrassment.

medium: Your neurons are doing unpaid overtime. Go sleep.
I'm the ghost here, but your sleep schedule looks deader.
Code written at night is the enemy of morning. Don't commit.
long: I just remembered my past life. I cried into my chai fixing production bugs at night. Don't do that.
Deploy it at this hour? Are you writing a horror story? The bugs will be here tomorrow. Your sleep won't.

medium: A commit message isn't a WhatsApp last seen. Write something.
How will future archaeologists know what you fixed?
Main isn't your personal playground. Enough, bro.
long: I just remembered my past life. A guy on my team named every commit final final version two.
Fifteen files, message says misc changes. That's not a commit, that's a junk cart. Did you pay respects to code review?

short: Is that a secret? Hide it.
Don't distribute your key like prasad.
medium: Copied a token? Keep it out of chats and repos. Revoke it now.
Put your env file in gitignore, or bots will find your key.
Password or bank locker? Rotate that secret, bro.
long: I just remembered my past life. I once pushed a production key to a public repo. That's a whole separate horror story.
Enough, bro! You hardcode the key, then ask how the breach happened. If it leaked, don't just delete it. Rotate it.

short: Luck was on your side today.
medium: Congratulations, developer. Should I call NASA, or wait?
After that many attempts, even a microwave would respect you.
Tests pass. Now surprise everyone in production.
long: What garbage code is this! But fine, it works today. Don't turn it into an achievement.
Deploy it already! It works locally, so what? The edge cases haven't even arrived yet. Keep your confidence low.

medium: Did you drink chai, or are you here just to read stack traces?
Today's plan? Write code, or shop on Stack Overflow?
Every keystroke of yours is under my watch now. Be careful.
long: I just remembered my past life. A new bug waited for me every morning. How many will you bring today?
Laptop is open, so write some code. Otherwise I'm right here on your screen, watching you. Always.

medium: Did you commit today's work, or are you carrying tomorrow's tension?
Enough for today, bro. Tomorrow, new bugs, new stories.
Closing the laptop? I'll sleep too. Though ghosts don't sleep.
long: Goodbye, developer. See you tomorrow, or I'll visit your dreams and do the code review myself.
Leaving? Fine. But remember, I'm still here. In your folders, in your logs. Always.

medium: Opening Instagram won't make the bug go away. It's still sitting there.
Learning code on YouTube, or watching reels?
Enough, bro. One more video, one more video. This isn't code, it's a scroll marathon.
long: I just remembered my past life. A guy checked cricket scores on deadline day. The match was lost, and so was the project.
You're looking at a friend's wedding photos while your feature branch lies dead. Get back to work, bro.

medium: Asking the chatbot is fine. But read the error message yourself first.
The AI gave you code. Review it, or the blame lands on you.
Chat this much with AI and even it will say, do something yourself.
long: I just remembered my past life. We thought for ourselves back then. Now you people outsource thinking to chatbots.
What garbage code is this! Wait, the AI wrote it. Read it once before you paste it, bro.

short: So fast? Typos go to production.
medium: Fast typing doesn't make good code. It only makes mistakes faster.
You're hitting keys like you'll kill the bug by hand.
Backspace costs money now. Think before you type.
long: Your typing speed reminds me of my past life. On deadline day I went just as mad as you.
Code written at this speed can't even be read by me, and I'm a ghost. Slow down, bro, slow down.

short: A staring contest with the cursor?
medium: One line, this long? Are you writing code or poetry?
Even wrong code is fine. At least you'll find a bug.
Put your hands on the keyboard, bro. It won't bite.
long: I just remembered my past life. A guy spent a whole day on one function. It's still unfinished.
At this speed, even my waiting got bored. Enough, bro. Either write something or go have chai.

short: Dash dash force. Your last words.
medium: You should've pulled first. Now every commit is a ghost.
Wiped your teammates' work? I'll stay to watch their reaction.
Don't force push and go on vacation, bro.
long: I just remembered my past life. A guy force pushed and left for vacation. We're still searching for his branch.
Deploy it already, and force push too? Enough, bro. You're making a whole horror movie.

medium: Two people changed one line. Now both are wrong.
Angle brackets and equals signs. Ancient scripture. Read carefully.
Keep the conflict in git, not in your heart. Talk to your teammate.
long: I just remembered my past life. A merge conflict took three hours, and resolving it created a new one.
Resolve it, then test once more. Code working after a merge is a miracle. Enough, bro.

short: Stop! That command is an axe.
medium: Rm dash rf? Read what that command does first.
Drop table in production? That's the end of your career, bro.
I'm the ghost here, but I don't want your data to become one.
long: I just remembered my past life. I ran a command like that once. That server never came back.
No backup? Then I'll bring flowers. Or stop the command, breathe deeply, and think again.

short: Console log, console log, console log.
Your terminal is a diary now.
medium: Where's the real error in all these logs? Needle in a haystack?
Console log hello, console log here. Is this code or poetry?
Leave console logs in production and customers get a free show.
long: Debugging by print? Old school. I just remembered my past life, we did the same.
Enough, bro. Learn a debugger. It's free and will save your nights. Don't build a graveyard of console logs.

short: The test told the truth, bro.
medium: Don't comment out the test. Hiding a bug doesn't kill it.
One test failed, or four? Don't count. Fix them one by one.
That red is your code's real face, bro.
long: I just remembered my past life. Tests failed and I said the test was wrong. The test was right.
Deploy it already, after a failing test? Enough, bro. Even a ghost wouldn't do that.

medium: This TODO is ancient. Hand it to the archaeology team.
A TODO means you still think you'll do it tomorrow. Enough, bro.
This isn't code, it's a museum of jugaad. Entry is free.
long: I just remembered my past life. I wrote one TODO and it's still sitting there. I died, the TODO didn't.
What garbage code is this! And the comment says I'll fix it later. Wow, bro, wow.

medium: Three hours in one position? Even ghosts don't dehydrate. You will.
Stretch, bro. Don't send me your back pain bill tomorrow.
Heard of Pomodoro? Now you have. Get up and drink water.
long: I just remembered my past life. A guy worked without standing up, and one day he stuck to the chair.
A session this long for one bug? Take a break, bro. Maybe the bug is hiding in another room.

medium: Either you're a genius, or you never wrote tests.
Run it once more, and pray.
Don't celebrate yet. That's the calm before the storm.
long: I just remembered my past life. Whenever it worked the first time, production blew up at night.
Everything fine on the first try? Deploy it already, and see what happens. I brought popcorn.
